title: How FDPM Thinks
subtitle: A conceptual architecture read of fdpm-cli
description: Plan for the August 2026 architecture snapshot of the fdpm-cli repository: what the reader must be able to predict after reading, which claims each part must land, and which repository files carry the evidence.

secondary: LLM agents onboarding to the MCP surface

thesis: FDPM is a single-writer event-sourced ledger for typed graphs whose agent-facing vocabulary has not yet caught up with its stated purpose.
success_criteria: A reader can predict the outcome of a novel MCP call from the thesis alone.
Every tension named in the report is anchored to a file and line or to a test run.
out_of_scope: Runtime performance characteristics of the JSONL log at scale.

content.claim: Every claim in the report is anchored to a repository file, a line range, or a live test run, and unanchored claims are marked as reasoned from code.
content.reasoning: The repository's own DISCLAIMER.md forbids unverifiable premises, so the report has to show its evidence discipline before it shows its findings.

sections.title: System thesis
sections.through_line: One ledger, two gates, pure replay: the whole system follows from three choices.

content.claim: FDPM is a single-writer, event-sourced ledger for typed graphs in which every mutation becomes one immutable operation from a closed set of twenty-three kinds.
content.reasoning: The operation kind enum is closed by spec, the store's append is the only write path, and the projection is discarded and rebuilt from the log on every load.
counter_arguments: Snapshots exist, so the log is not the only state on disk.

content.claim: Two gates stand between a proposed mutation and the log: the per-kind payload schema and the seven-step validation pipeline run on the proposed post-state.
content.reasoning: Rejection never reaches the log because the host validates before it appends; deletes are the documented exception and rely on apply-time rollback instead.

sections.title: Surfaces
sections.through_line: Five fronts, one host, one file on disk: the coordination story is the file's stat tuple.

content.claim: The LLM reaches the ledger only through a thirty-tool, three-tier manifest whose authorization happens at dispatch time rather than at advertisement time.
Cross-process coordination is detection by file stat, not exclusion by lock, so two one-shot writers can still race to the same revision.
content.reasoning: The session records an mtime and size tuple per workbook log and refuses writes when it changes; nothing serialises the append itself.
counter_arguments: A single operator on a laptop rarely runs two writers at once.

sections.title: The gap between purpose and code

content.claim: The verb, resource, prompt and expression vocabulary that PURPOSE describes as the reason the architecture exists is not yet in the code.
content.reasoning: The operation kind set is closed to plugins, no prompt registration exists, and the plugin-tool discovery function returns an empty list unconditionally.
counter_arguments: The README status table already marks these surfaces as roadmap milestones rather than shipped features.

content.claim: Each finding maps to a file path and line range in the repository at commit 78c7ff7, listed in the order the findings appear.
